addition.title: Addition
addition.subtitle: Learn to add numbers quickly
addition.explanation: Add left to right instead of right to left: add the tens of the second number to the first, then add the remaining units. There's no decomposition trick beyond that — the in-game Hint button won't do anything here.

multiplication.title: Multiplication
multiplication.subtitle: Master mental multiplication
multiplication.explanation: Multiply left to right too: multiply the tens of the larger operand by the other one, then the units, and add the two results. This is exactly the Hint you'll see in-game if you get stuck.

squaring2d.title: Squaring (2 digits)
squaring2d.subtitle: Square 2-digit numbers
squaring2d.explanation: Use x² = (x−a)(x+a) + a², choosing a so that x−a and x+a land on numbers you can multiply easily — usually the nearest multiple of ten. This is the same Hint shown in-game.

squaring3d.title: Squaring (3 digits)
squaring3d.subtitle: Handle 3-digit squares
squaring3d.explanation: Same identity, but round to the nearest hundred instead of ten — a is now a two-digit number. Since a² isn't trivial anymore, apply the same trick to a itself, this time rounding it to the nearest ten.

squaring4d.title: Squaring (4 digits)
squaring4d.subtitle: Master 4-digit squares
squaring4d.explanation: Round to the nearest thousand this time. The correction a is now three digits, so squaring it recurses one level deeper — and holding onto its square while you finish the rest of the calculation is exactly where the Major System earns its keep.

majorSystem.title: Major System
majorSystem.subtitle: Learn the Major System step by step
majorSystem.explanation: Each digit maps to one or more consonant sounds. String together the consonants for a number's digits, in order, then fill in any vowels you like to spell a real word — vowels carry no value. A memorable word is far easier to hold onto than a bare string of digits. The mapping below is tuned to Spanish consonant sounds, so the example words only work in Spanish — the same reason the game's own "rhymed-order" finding is Spanish-specific.

1.note: This one's trickier — the units add up to more than 10.
a rounds to the nearest hundred either way — up here, down in the first example.

0.note: "lógica" is a real Spanish word — the whole point of the Major System is picking a word that means something, not just any consonant string.

liveNote.squaring3d: The live example below shows a simpler one-step version — round to the nearest ten instead of a hundred — which works for any digit count but produces less round factors than the full technique above.
liveNote.squaring4d: The live example below shows a simpler one-step version — round to the nearest ten instead of a thousand — which works for any digit count but skips the Major System step.
